title: world.counters gpu reports the world's view as a render-graph instance of the sdf.world passes, pass by pass in order, rendered once for a still world and identically on both backends
binding: The positive leg boots a still offscreen world with one SDF view, waits for the engine to be ready (world.wait ready: the world's residency has built its tables and the root has rendered over the world's first output), and reads the gpu section of world.counters sixty completed ticks later and again after thirty more. The world's view is the render-graph instance world, whose node renders the sdf.world package's eleven passes; the residency's uploads read as sdf:world, its fillers pass executing, its bricks pass skipped, since the world bakes no brick, its upload pass executing, and its environment pass executing with its two dispatches, since the default sky fogs and its environment map has not rendered before; the still sky never renders it again. Nothing the view renders from changes in a still world, so the scheduler lets its first render stand for every later frame: the world node's submission is the same in both reads, while the root, main, renders every frame, so its second read carries a later submission. The world node's pass lines appear in the fragment's order, mask through composite, each carrying the barriers the planner planned for it, the write of its pass block, and the march steps and texels written its kernels counted, and none a command buffer: every pass records into the node's one list a frame, which the outside line counts; the mesh pass skips the frame, because the world draws no mesh, so its line reads skipped rather than a count of zero and its target and depth take no barrier; the ambient and shadow passes skip it too, because the world leaves ambient occlusion and soft shadows off, so their lines read skipped. The cull arguments pass marches nothing and writes no texel, so it counts zero of both. The sky and the composite write their pass group's descriptors during their first recording, once for the slot, a filler at each of the 32 screen slots their layers may sample among them, so this frame's lines carry those writes; the sky evaluates its field runs at every one of the 4096 output pixels, since no pixel of the view is wholly covered with all eight of its neighbours, and the composite counts each pixel it writes. The sky's detail rows are its three field runs, then one per layer label: the default stack holds only the gradient, so the gradient row carries the 4096 evaluations, the lowest run's row the 4096 texels it writes, and the upper runs' rows nothing; the composite evaluates no sky, since its fog reads the environment map, and its lowest run's row counts the one base tap each of its 4096 pixels loads, since a stack with no upper field run samples no upper run image. The CPU device-sealed upload law holds the first frame to 432 host-visible bytes for mask, 436 for beam, cull-args, primary and surface, 440 for views, and 456 for sky and composite. Views writes the additional four-byte sky detail-row index used by analytic panels. Every executed line ends with environment.projections, environment.projection-texels and environment.skipped, all zero in these view and root passes because candidate projection belongs to the residency's environment pass. The detail row word follows the row word in the block so a hit pass's changed words form no more runs than they did before named rows; the region's run list is bounded, and one run more would merge its neighbours across the words between them and re-send those. Those pass lines are exact on Vulkan and Direct3D 12 alike, which is the cross-backend proof. The residency's upload line, the work outside the passes and the created buffers, pools and sets follow the device's residency policy (a staging device records copies, transitions and copy sets beside the writes), so the canary names those lines without pinning them. Neither node creates a pipeline or a shader module: every pipeline counts under gpu.pass-pipelines, nineteen pipelines and twenty-one shader modules (the fourteen SDF kernels the world's residency leases, the brick baker absent from the counters kernels, the device's region copy, the one place pipeline the root's four place passes share, the mesh pass's graphics pipeline with its vertex and fragment modules, and the impostor card pipeline the residency leases beside it even in a world that draws no card, a graphics pipeline of its own whose cache entry creates its own vertex module from the mesh pass's vertex stage and its card fragment module). The residency creates two images, its sampled and storage fillers, and the world node ten (its output in each of three frame slots, and, one each, which every frame slot shares, the mesh pass's visibility target and depth, the lit image views writes, and the sky's four run images, the lowest run's and three upper runs'). The root places the world's one view through its four place passes, none of which shows anything, so none dispatches, and each pass line carries only its planned barriers and counts no march step and no texel. The discriminating leg reads world.counters gpu twice before the first tick, when no submission has completed, so neither read shows a pass line and the positive's exact lines turn red.
